title: Finite type lifts along a nilpotent ideal (ring version)
statement: Let $A'\to B'$ be a ring map of commutative rings and $I\subseteq A'$ a nilpotent ideal ($I^{n+1}=0$ for some $n\ge0$). If the induced ring map $A'/I\to B'/IB'$ is of finite type (i.e. $B'/IB'$ is a finitely generated $A'/I$-algebra), then $A'\to B'$ is of finite type. (Proof: choose $b_1,\dots,b_m\in B'$ whose images generate $B'/IB'$ over $A'/I$, let $R=A'[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'$, $x_j\mapsto b_j$; then $R/IR=(A'/I)[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'/IB'$ is surjective, i.e. $B'=N+IB'$ for the image $N$ of $R$, viewed as $R$-modules with $IR$ nilpotent; by Nakayama's lemma for a nilpotent ideal (Algebra 00DV (11): $M=IM$ with $I$ nilpotent implies $M=0$, applied to $M=B'/N$) $R\to B'$ is surjective.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW (label lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian), proof, 'The translation of (2) into algebra' (stated there with I^2=0; the argument uses only Algebra, Lemma 00DV (label lemma-NAK) part (11), which holds for any nilpotent I)
